$comment: Yahoo Fantasy Sports API capability matrix for the Dinkel Portal.
This file is not documentation — it is read at runtime by
@dinkel/challenge-engine and the API to decide what the portal is allowed to
do. A challenge whose required capability is not 'verified' here stays
BLOCKED and no math runs for it. That is the mechanism that prevents the
documented        - stated in current official Yahoo documentation
documented-legacy - only in the archived/unofficial mirror of the old guide
inferred          - widely used by third-party clients, not in current docs
untested          - never exercised against a real Yahoo league
mock-only         - exercised against apps/mock-yahoo fixtures only
verified          - exercised successfully against a real Yahoo league
failed            - exercised and did not behave as documented
Update testStatus ONLY from an actual observed request. Run
`npm run verify:yahoo` after Yahoo grants credentials; it prints the
capability keys it was able to confirm.

notes: Access is granted after Yahoo reviews an application: 'Our team reviews every submission and will reach out with next steps, including credentials and onboarding resources.'
'Access to the Yahoo Fantasy Sports API is read-only by default.' Read/write requires separate justification, which this portal does not request.
The former guide at developer.yahoo.com/fantasysports/guide/ now 308-redirects to a landing page. Current docs: https://sports.yahoo.com/developer/docs/

A Fantasy-Sports-specific Terms of Use is referenced at legal.yahoo.com/us/en/yahoo/terms/product-atos/fantasysportsapi/index.html but returned HTTP 404 on 2026-07-26. The binding 'API Access and Use Agreement' is presented inside the application flow, so its full text must be read at application time and this file updated accordingly.
Token responses return a new access_token and may return a new refresh_token. The client treats rotation as expected and persists whichever refresh token comes back.
redirect_uri must match a value registered on the Yahoo app exactly. Yahoo requires HTTPS, so local development uses a self-signed certificate rather than plain http://localhost.
'oob' (out of band) is documented for apps without browser access. Not used here.

'You may not retain or use, and must immediately remove from any Application and any data repository in your possession or under your control any Yahoo user data obtained through the Yahoo APIs that is not explicitly identified as being storable indefinitely in the API Documents within 24 hours after the time at which you obtained the data.'

The general terms defer the storable-indefinitely list to the API Documents. Public summaries identify GUID and authenticated token value. This portal treats that list as exhaustive and stores nothing else Yahoo-derived beyond the TTL'd cache.
Prohibited-use categories include 'gambling or gambling items'. Dues and prizes are tracked strictly as internal administrative records; the portal processes no payments and takes no share.
Monetization requires prior express written permission. This portal is noncommercial.

Yahoo's API terms list 'gambling or gambling items' among prohibited uses, and require written permission for monetization. Dues and prizes here are the league's own administrative records: no Yahoo data appears on them, no payment processor is integrated, no funds are held or moved, and the portal takes no share.

A payout record is ALWAYS created deliberately by a commissioner. Nothing generates a money record from a finalized challenge or any other Yahoo-derived outcome — automating that would make the pipeline resemble an automated stakes engine, and it saves nobody any work.
A challenge result is not payable until a commissioner finalizes it, so a person always stands between Yahoo's numbers and a prize.
`paymentMethod` (cash, venmo, zelle, paypal, check, other) is descriptive of what happened elsewhere. It is never executable and triggers nothing.
The interface avoids gambling vocabulary entirely — no odds, lines, bets, wagers, stakes, or 'winnings'. The language is dues, prize, payout, owed, settled.

The fantasy-specific terms URL currently 404s and the binding agreement appears inside the approval flow, which has not been seen. This section records the position taken, not a confirmed reading of an unseen document.
The current documentation describes GET operations only. No POST, PUT, or DELETE operation is documented for any resource.
Consequently the portal performs NO Yahoo mutation of any kind. Setting draft order, editing rosters, processing transactions, and commissioner actions are all treated as unsupported.

Third-party wrapper libraries expose add/drop/trade helpers, which implies undocumented write endpoints exist. Those are deliberately not used: undocumented private endpoints are out of scope by policy.
No documented endpoint performs a commissioner action.
Read/write OAuth permission would not constitute evidence that commissioner actions are supported, and this portal requests read-only regardless.
The LLWS workflow therefore produces a printable draft order for manual entry in Yahoo's own interface.

resources.feature: List the authenticated user's fantasy football leagues
resources.commissionerBehavior: none — returns the signed-in user's own leagues
limitations: Current docs list `/users;use_login=1` as a resource but do not spell out the games/leagues sub-resource chain. The `;game_codes=nfl` filter and the `/leagues` sub-resource come from the archived guide and universal third-party usage.
Whether a league the user was removed from still appears is unverified.
Requires runtime confirmation of the exact nesting before being relied on.

resources.feature: League name, season, scoring type, week structure
resources.commissionerBehavior: none observed — settings are readable by any league member
limitations: Field-level shape is unverified; the parser tolerates missing optional fields rather than assuming them.
Whether private-league settings differ for non-commissioner members is unverified.

resources.feature: Teams in the league and their managers
resources.commissionerBehavior: unverified whether manager email or GUID visibility differs for a commissioner
limitations: Manager display names and team names returned here are Yahoo user data: cached under TTL and never persisted.
Whether manager GUIDs are exposed for all teams or only the authenticated user's is unverified. The portal does not depend on other managers' GUIDs.

resources.feature: Per-team fantasy points for a week
limitations: Scoreboard is listed as a league sub-resource in current docs without field detail.
Live in-progress values differ from final values, and Yahoo issues stat corrections days later. Anything computed from this stays provisional until the correction window closes.

resources.feature: Which roster slot each player occupied, including bench
resources.commissionerBehavior: unverified whether a commissioner may read other teams' historical rosters that a member cannot
limitations: The bench indicator is conventionally selected_position = 'BN', and IR is 'IR'. Unverified against a real league.
Whether a past week's roster is retrievable after the season ends is unverified — this matters for recalculating an old challenge.
Reading every team's roster is one request per team, which has rate-limit implications that are undocumented.
Per-player points come from the roster read when Yahoo includes them; when absent the portal shows a dash rather than computing a substitute.

resources.feature: A player's fantasy points for a week under league scoring
limitations: League-context scoring is required: game-context stats would not reflect Dinkel's scoring settings.
Whether points come back as a computed total or must be derived from raw stats and league scoring settings is unverified. The latter would be materially more work.
Batch size limits for player_keys are undocumented; the client pages conservatively.

resources.feature: Individual raw stat values by Yahoo stat id
limitations: Stat ids are numeric and league-specific in meaning. There is no current official published mapping of stat id to stat name; the /game/{game_key}/stat_categories resource is the conventional source and is itself only in the archived guide.
Receptions, passing yards, and touchdown counts all depend on this. Any challenge requiring them stays BLOCKED until a real league confirms both the endpoint and the id mapping.

resources.feature: Projected fantasy points for a player or team in a week
limitations: No current or archived official documentation found for projected points as an API field. Yahoo's website displays projections, but that is not evidence of an API field.
Scraping the website to obtain projections is out of scope by policy.
Every projection-dependent challenge is therefore BLOCKED, not estimated.
Displayed live only. Not persisted — a Dinkel-owned final finish order is recorded at season close so draft-order tiebreakers survive without retained Yahoo data.

resources.feature: Adds, drops, trades, and waiver activity
resources.commissionerBehavior: unverified whether commissioner-executed transactions are distinguishable in the response
limitations: Read and displayed live only; never persisted.
`transaction_data` is returned as a bare object for a single move and as a numeric-keyed collection for an add/drop pair. The parser handles both; which shape a real league returns is unverified.
The `;count=` limit is applied but its documented maximum is unknown, so the portal asks for 25 rather than attempting to page the full season.
No write operation is documented for transactions, so the portal reads them and offers no way to create one.
Read-only. There is no documented way to WRITE a draft order, which is why the LLWS workflow ends in manual entry.
Displayed live only; Dinkel's own draft history comes from the CSV import instead.
No published rate limit was found in current official documentation.
The client therefore behaves conservatively regardless: retry with exponential backoff and jitter, honour Retry-After, cap concurrency, and cache aggressively within the 24-hour ceiling.
Because per-team roster reads are N requests for N teams, a full-league challenge calculation is the heaviest operation in the portal and is scheduled rather than run on page load.
